findings.reason: a worker implementing §2 as written will find one of the four refusals has no backend to judge, and will either silently judge it against the wrong lane or drop it; the plan sentence needs to say which, or narrow the claim to the three refusals that are node-local.
findings.text: §2 says all four `plan_dispatch` refusals "move into one function ... that both paths call, and each batch entry's node is judged by it, with the same locked decisions and budget ceiling", but the fourth of them — the execution-fit refusal at `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:869` — is judged from `execution_fit = capability.assess_execution_fit(node.done_when, role=..., execution_capable=backend.get("execution_capable"))`, where `backend` is the backend `plan_dispatch` resolves for the node's role and section (`dispatch_plan.py:752`/`:770`). The queue path, `queue_requests` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:293`), is handed only a lane name (`backend_name`, defaulting to the config's local/default backend) and never resolves role or section routing, because the queued request is routed later by the picker. Sharing that refusal therefore either judges execution fit against a lane the node may never run on — a different input from the single path, so "the same refusal detail" is false for it — or forces the queue to resolve routing at queue time, which is a behaviour change §2 does not declare and which the section's own "the rest of the batch is stored as today" forbids.

findings.reason: the measure is what a worker optimises to; without a case per shared refusal, a worker can satisfy the gate while sharing two refusals of four, and the plan's central claim would ship untested.
findings.text: §2's done-when exercises the shared function with two cases only: the goal-conjunction refusal (`validate_node`) and the missing negative control (`negative_control_finding`). Its negative controls are "removing the batch's contract call" and "calling `validate_node` alone stores the fourth case's entry", so if the batch called `validate_node` plus `negative_control_finding` and nothing else, every case in the measure would pass. The `gate_population_finding` and execution-fit refusals — two of the four the deliverable names — are never exercised, so "the call is shared rather than copied: ... so the two cannot drift" is unmeasured for half the contract, and the gate cannot show that the drift the section exists to prevent is prevented.

response_events.note: §2 now shares the three node-local refusals (validate_node, negative_control_finding, gate_population_finding); the execution-fit refusal stays at launch because a queued request's lane is chosen later by the picker, and the section says so.
